```{python}
import scanpy as sc
import pandas as pd
```

```{python}
adata = sc.read_h5ad("wu2021_brca.h5ad")   # log-normalized

basal = ["CID4515", "CID44971", "CID4465", "CID4495"]
solid = ["CID4515", "CID44971"]
sub = adata[adata.obs["orig.ident"].isin(basal)].copy()
```

```{python}
fao_genes = [
    "ACAA2", "ACACB", "ACAD10", "ACAD11", "ACADL", "ACADM", "ACADS",
    "ACADSB", "ACADVL", "ACAT1", "ACOT11", "ACSF2", "ACSL1", "ACSL6",
    "ACSM1", "ACSM2A", "ACSM2B", "ACSM3", "ACSM4", "ACSM5", "ACSS1",
    "AMACR", "CPT1A", "CPT1B", "CPT1C", "CPT2", "CRAT", "CROT",
    "DECR1", "ECHS1", "ECI1", "ECI2", "ETFA", "ETFB", "ETFDH",
    "HADH", "HADHA", "HADHB", "HSD17B10", "MCEE", "MMUT", "PCCA",
    "PCCB", "SLC25A20"
]
```

```{python}
df = pd.DataFrame({"gene": fao_genes})
df.to_csv("fao_genes.csv", index=False)
```

```{python}
#FAO gene set from the TCGA analysis (MitoPathways FAO)
fao_genes = pd.read_csv("fao_genes.csv")["gene"].tolist() 
fao_genes = [g for g in fao_genes if g in sub.var_names]
print("FAO genes found:", len(fao_genes))
```

```{python}
sc.tl.score_genes(sub, fao_genes, score_name="FAO_score")
```

```{python}
# Which myeloid / T cell labels exist? (needed to pick the M2 / CD8 groups)
print(sub.obs["celltype_major"].value_counts())
print(sub.obs["celltype_minor"].value_counts())
```

```{python}
# Mean FAO per cell type, per patient, with cell counts
g = sub.obs.groupby(["celltype_major", "orig.ident"])["FAO_score"]
tab = pd.concat([g.mean().round(3).rename("mean_FAO"),
                 g.size().rename("n_cells")], axis=1).reset_index()
print(tab.pivot(index="celltype_major", columns="orig.ident",
                values=["mean_FAO", "n_cells"]))
```

```{python}
pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", None)

print("FAO genes found:", len(fao_genes))

mean_tab = tab.pivot(index="celltype_major", columns="orig.ident", values="mean_FAO")
n_tab = tab.pivot(index="celltype_major", columns="orig.ident", values="n_cells")
print(mean_tab.round(3))
print(n_tab)

# The labels we need to pick macrophage and CD8 groups
mm = sub[sub.obs["celltype_major"].isin(["Myeloid", "T-cells"])]
print(mm.obs["celltype_minor"].value_counts())
```

```{python}
# Overall picture
sc.pl.violin(sub, "FAO_score", groupby="celltype_major", rotation=90)
```

```{python}
# genes missing from the dataset
all_fao = pd.read_csv("fao_genes.csv")["gene"].tolist()
print("Missing:", [g for g in all_fao if g not in sub.var_names])

# FAO by minor cell type, in the 4 Basal patients
keep = ["Macrophage", "Monocyte", "DCs", "T cells CD8+", "T cells CD4+"]
m = sub[sub.obs["celltype_minor"].isin(keep)]
g = m.obs.groupby(["celltype_minor", "orig.ident"])["FAO_score"]
tab = pd.concat([g.mean().round(3).rename("mean_FAO"),
                 g.size().rename("n_cells")], axis=1).reset_index()
print(tab.pivot(index="celltype_minor", columns="orig.ident",
                values=["mean_FAO", "n_cells"]))
```

In bulk TCGA, tumors with high FAO (fatty acid oxidation) also have more M2 macrophages and CD8 T cells. The open question was whether that’s because the immune cells themselves carry FAO genes, or because the tumor cells are doing the FAO.

Using single-cell data from 4 Basal-like patients, the answer is mostly the tumor cells:

- Cancer cells had the highest FAO score in every patient.

- Macrophages were slightly above other myeloid cells, but far below the cancer cells.

- T cells were at or below background.

Limitation:

- Only 4 patients, two of them low confidence

- It shows where the signal comes from, but it can’t test the correlation with M2 or CD8 itself

- There is no M2 label in this dataset
